claims.claim: The person registering the death must be a qualified informant.
claims.quote: Qualified informants can register a death.
claims.note: An English council page states that qualified informants register a death.

claims.claim: A relative of the deceased can be a qualified informant.
claims.quote: A qualified informant can be: A relative A person who was present at the death
claims.note: A relative is listed as a qualified informant.

claims.claim: Someone present at the death can be a qualified informant.
claims.quote: A qualified informant can be: A relative A person who was present at the death
claims.note: A person present at the death is listed as a qualified informant.

claims.claim: An administrator of the premises where the death occurred can be a qualified informant.
claims.quote: Occupier of the house / home where the death happened - if in an establishment the occupier could be the establishment's manager or senior administrator
claims.note: An English council page lists the establishment's manager or senior administrator as someone who can register.

claims.claim: Registration is required for every death in England and Wales.
claims.quote: All deaths must be registered at the Register Office for the area where death occurred within 5 days of the Registrar receiving the completed paperwork.
claims.note: An English council page states all deaths must be registered; this is a general rule of registration in England.

claims.claim: Registration must be done by a qualified informant such as a relative or a person present at the death.
claims.quote: A qualified informant can be: A relative A person who was present at the death
claims.note: Qualified informants, including relatives and people present at the death, register a death.

claims.claim: The death must be registered within 5 days.
claims.quote: Register the death within 5 days (8 days in Scotland) of getting the confirmation.
claims.note: GOV.UK states 5 days, counted from the medical examiner's confirmation.
